items.title: Valero Energy Q2: Revenue $44.48B Beat, EPS $12.54 Crushes Estimates, Refining Profit Surges 247% on Tight Supply
items.summary: Valero Energy (VLO) reported record second-quarter revenue of $44.48 billion and adjusted EPS of $12.54, significantly beating analyst estimates due to strong refining margins and global supply imbalances. The company saw its net income surge by 419% year-over-year to $3.7 billion and returned $2.6 billion to shareholders, increasing its dividend to $1.20 per share. While structural refining dynamics suggest a higher margin floor, potential economic slowdowns and geopolitical shifts impacting oil production pose key risks to future performance.

items.title: Trump Media & Technology Group (NASDAQ: DJT) Faces New Investor Questions As Canada Tariff Pause Reshapes Trade Outlook
items.summary: Trump Media & Technology Group (DJT) is under fresh investor scrutiny after the US temporarily suspended tariffs on Canadian imports. While the company's financial figures show limited direct impact from tariffs due to low revenue and significant net losses, investors are focusing on its political connections and potential digital trade alignment in future US-Canada agreements. The broader market context highlights the intertwining of trade policy and political branding for companies like Trump Media.

items.title: Pembina Approves Greenlight Power Project for AI Data Centers
items.summary: Pembina Pipeline Corporation has approved the Greenlight Electricity Center (GLEC) project in Alberta, a significant energy infrastructure development. This project, a collaboration with Morgan Stanley Infrastructure Partners and Kineticor Asset Management, will supply dedicated electricity to a hyperscale data center, generating long-term fee-based earnings for Pembina. The GLEC will utilize advanced combined cycle technology and operate under a long-term commercial agreement, supporting Alberta's growing digital economy and AI investments.

items.title: Berkshire Hathaway stock holds above $743,000 as Buffett reshapes the portfolio
items.summary: Berkshire Hathaway's Class A stock is trading above $743,000, reflecting its status as a high-priced but widely followed investment vehicle. Recent portfolio adjustments include reducing stakes in Bank of America while benefiting from energy holdings like Occidental Petroleum, aligning with Buffett's capital allocation strategy. The article highlights Berkshire's defensive qualities amidst broader debt concerns and elevated interest rates, positioning it as a hedge against macroeconomic risks.

items.title: Fed Approves NatWest Office in Connecticut
items.summary: The Federal Reserve has approved National Westminster Bank Plc's application to establish a representative office in Stamford, Connecticut. This office will allow NatWest to engage with U.S. customers and promote services but will not permit full banking operations like accepting deposits or making loans. This approval expands NatWest's existing presence in Stamford, complementing NatWest Markets' operations, and is subject to continued regulatory oversight by both federal and state authorities.

items.title: Why I Think the Best Dividend Stock Isn't a Tech Name: It's Realty Income
items.summary: The article argues that Realty Income (NYSE: O), a real estate investment trust (REIT), is a better dividend stock than tech giants like Microsoft or Apple. While tech stocks offer dividend growth, Realty Income provides a higher yield (over 5%) and dependable monthly dividend payments that have consistently increased over time. Its stable cash flow, conservative payout ratio, and strong balance sheet make it an ideal choice for passive income investors.
